title: ByteWolf Vision Detection Event v0.1
description: One detection in one camera frame, as the Vision stack publishes it to consumers (the Cognitive Runtime, its perception hooks, the world model and the dashboard). It is observation-only: it describes what was seen, never a command, and it is a consumer-facing view -- the producing model's internal frame details (calibration, latency, drop counters) stay inside Vision. Consumers resolve freshness themselves: see docs and brain/vision/canonical.py.

contract_version.description: Pins the meaning of every field below. A consumer that does not know this version rejects the event rather than guess.

event_id.description: Unique id for this detection, so it can be correlated with a summary, an artifact or an audit record.

source.description: What produced it, e.g. 'camera:front_rgb' or 'camera:down_rgb'. Names the sensor origin for audit; never for dispatch.

observed_at.description: RFC 3339, UTC, with an explicit offset. When the frame was captured -- age is measured from here, not from publish time, so a slow pipeline cannot hide behind a fresh publish.

max_age_s.description: How long this detection stays usable after observed_at. Past it the detection is stale and must not be acted on, even though its values are still present.

validity.description: What the producer knows. 'valid': trustworthy at observed_at. 'invalid': measured but not trusted. 'missing': no detection was made. 'stale' is not declared here; only the consumer knows the current time, so it derives staleness from age.

model_id.description: The detector model that produced this, e.g. 'yolo' or 'rt-detr'.

model_version.description: The model's version, so a regression is attributable and a consumer can pin.

label.description: The detected class, e.g. 'person'. Not an authorisation: 'person' is never 'authorized_operator'; identity is a separate, opt-in pipeline.

frame.description: The frame's pixel dimensions, so a consumer can interpret the bounding box. The producer's richer internal CameraFrame (device, calibration, latency, drop counters) is deliberately not exposed here.

bounding_box.description: Pixel box, origin top-left. The loader also checks it lies within the frame (x_px + width_px <= frame.width_px, likewise for height), which JSON Schema cannot express across fields.

artifact_ref.description: An optional reference to a stored evidence clip or keyframe for this detection's frame.

payload_hash.description: sha256 of the artifact payload, so a consumer can verify the clip it references.
